# AML Compiler Output — dist/

This directory contains generated output artifacts produced by the AML compiler pipeline.

The files inside `/dist` demonstrate the full semantic transformation process from AML source code into accountable rendered output.

---

# Compiler Pipeline

```text
AML Source
   ↓
Lexer
   ↓
Parser
   ↓
Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
   ↓
Abstract Meaning Tree (AMT)
   ↓
EthicalRenderGate Evaluation
   ↓
Semantic HTML Generation
```

---

# Generated Files

## tokens.json

Lexical analysis output generated by the AML lexer.

Contains:
- token classification
- source positions
- keyword detection
- lexical structure metadata

Example token types:
- KEYWORD
- IDENTIFIER
- STRING
- NUMBER
- LEFT_BRACE
- RIGHT_BRACE

---

## ast.json

Abstract Syntax Tree generated by the AML parser.

Represents:
- hierarchical program structure
- semantic blocks
- properties
- nested runtime constructs

The AST preserves program structure before semantic expansion into the AMT.

---

## amt.json

Abstract Meaning Tree generated by the AML semantic compiler.

The AMT extends beyond syntax and preserves:
- semantic intent
- restoration metadata
- runtime meaning structures
- coherence relationships
- memory roles
- user-effect annotations

The AMT is the canonical semantic representation of an AML document.

---

## render_decision.json

Generated EthicalRenderGate evaluation output.

Each renderable element is evaluated using:

```aml
render_allowed =
  restoration_value >= attention_cost
```

The file includes:
- attention scoring
- restoration scoring
- render permissions
- fallback triggers
- accountability metadata
- runtime timestamps

This creates inspectable and auditable rendering behavior.

---

## index.html

Compiled semantic HTML output generated from AML source.

The generated output includes:
- semantic AML metadata
- restoration-aware rendering
- EthicalRenderGate-approved structures
- runtime-compatible data attributes
- meaning-preserving semantic rendering

This represents the final render stage of the AML compiler pipeline.

---

# Purpose of dist/

The `/dist` directory exists to demonstrate:
- compiler transparency
- semantic accountability
- inspectable rendering
- deterministic transformation
- meaning-preserving compilation

Traditional rendering systems expose very little of the decision process.

AML exposes the full semantic pipeline.

---

# AML Philosophy

Traditional web systems ask:

> Can this render?

AML introduces a second question:

> Should this render?

The AML compiler pipeline is designed to preserve:
- coherence
- clarity
- meaning
- accountability
- restoration value

through every transformation stage.
